Name: AfdDisableAddressSharing

Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'System Services Afd DisableAddressSharing' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Hardens the Ancillary Function Driver (AFD) by disabling socket address sharing, reducing local socket-hijacking opportunities.
Change Risk Level: Low - Low-level network-stack hardening; minimal application impact.

Name: AllowAnonymousSIDOrNameTranslation

Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member

Security Impact: Disables anonymous SID-to-name translation, preventing unauthenticated callers from mapping SIDs to account names for reconnaissance.
Change Risk Level: Low - Standard hardening; rarely affects domain operations.

Security Impact: Restricts loading of custom security packages into LSASS, reducing the chance of malicious authentication packages harvesting credentials.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Validate legitimate third-party SSP/AP before enforcing.

Name: AllowedToFormatAndEjectRemovableMedia
Control Name: Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Devices: Allowed to format and eject removable media' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Restricts which users may format and eject removable media interactively, limiting console-side data-handling to authorized roles.
Change Risk Level: Low - Affects interactive media handling; minimal impact.

Name: AllowICMPRedirectOverrideOSPF
Control Name: MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'MSS: (EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Legacy MSS network/kernel hardening '(EnableICMPRedirect) Allow ICMP redirects to override OSPF generated routes'. Tightens older TCP/IP and DLL-search behaviors (source routing, NetBIOS name release, DLL search order) to the recommended safer values.
Change Risk Level: Low - Long-standing hardening values; minimal modern compatibility impact.

Name: AllowLocalSystemNULLSessionFallback
Control Name: Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Disables NULL-session fallback for the LocalSystem account (set to 0), so LocalSystem can no longer fall back to unauthenticated null-credential NTLM sessions. This removes an anonymous authentication path that could be used for credential-less enumeration or relay.
Change Risk Level: Low - Disabling null-session fallback rarely affects modern services; validate legacy apps that rely on anonymous LocalSystem connections.

Name: AllowLocalSystemToUseComputerIdentityForNTLM
Control Name: Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Network security: Allow Local System to use computer identity for NTLM' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Configures whether Local System uses the computer identity for NTLM, ensuring consistent, expected service authentication behavior.
Change Risk Level: Low - Standard authentication behavior; minimal impact.

Name: AllowPKU2UAuthenticationAllowOnlineID
Control Name: Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Network Security: Allow PKU2U authentication requests to this computer to use online identities' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Allows this computer to accept PKU2U authentication requests that use online identities (the baseline sets AllowOnlineID to 1). Although STIG/CIS historically disable PKU2U, this baseline intentionally enables it because failover clustering relies on PKU2U for node-to-node authentication using Microsoft-trusted online identities. Setting it to 0 would confine authentication to domain/AD identities and can break cluster node communication and other online-identity peer logons.
Change Risk Level: Low - Changing to disabled can break failover-cluster node or online-identity authentication scenarios; validate before deviating.

Name: AllowPrintSpoolerClientConnections
Control Name: Allow Print Spooler to accept client connections
Availability: Domain Controller
Description: Controls whether the Print Spooler accepts remote client connections. Setting to 2 prevents exploitation vectors like PrintNightmare.
Security Impact: Prevents the Print Spooler from accepting remote client connections, mitigating PrintNightmare-class remote spooler abuse while preserving local printing.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Host cannot act as a print server; validate shared-printer needs.

Name: DeviceGuardRequireMicrosoftSignedBootChain
Control Name: Secured-Core Require MicrosoftSignedBootChain
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Secured-Core Require MicrosoftSignedBootChain' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires a Microsoft-signed UEFI Secure Boot chain as a Virtualization-Based Security prerequisite (value 1), so firmware and early-boot components are signature-verified before the OS loads. This anchors the hardware root of trust for VBS, HVCI, and Credential Guard and blocks bootkits and unsigned boot-level code from gaining pre-OS persistence. Setting 0 removes the requirement, allowing VBS to initialize without a verified boot chain.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Gates VBS/Credential Guard on a Microsoft-signed Secure Boot chain; hardware with Secure Boot disabled or unsigned boot components will not activate VBS until firmware is reconfigured. Confirm Secure Boot posture before enforcing.

Name: DeviceGuardRequirePlatformSecurityFeatures
Control Name: Secured-Core Require Platform Security (Secure Boot, DMA)
Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures '"Secured-Core Require Platform Security (Secure Boot, DMA)"' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires platform security features before Virtualization-Based Security activates: Secure Boot (1), or Secure Boot with DMA protection (3). This establishes the hardware root of trust that VBS, HVCI, and Credential Guard depend on, and value 3 additionally blocks malicious DMA-capable peripherals from reading protected memory. A lower or cleared value lets VBS run without verified platform protections, weakening the isolation those features provide.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Gates VBS on Secure Boot, or Secure Boot plus DMA protection at value 3; devices lacking Secure Boot or IOMMU/DMA-remapping will not start VBS until platform support is confirmed. Validate hardware capabilities before enforcing.

Name: DeviceGuardRequireUEFIMemoryAttributesTable

Availability: Domain Controller, Member Server, Workgroup Member
Description: Configures 'Secured-Core Require UEFI Memory Attribute Table' per security baseline requirements to enforce organizational security policy.
Security Impact: Requires UEFI firmware to publish a Memory Attributes Table (value 1) so firmware runtime memory is marked non-executable or read-only. HVCI relies on the MAT to extend code-integrity and memory protections over firmware regions; without it HVCI cannot constrain firmware memory, leaving a gap that could be used to bypass kernel code integrity. Setting 0 permits HVCI to run on firmware lacking these guarantees.
Change Risk Level: Medium - Requires UEFI firmware to publish a Memory Attributes Table for HVCI; firmware without MAT support prevents HVCI activation until updated. Check firmware/UEFI versions before enforcing.
